tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	# Issue #230: a web control surface on the remote port — investigation notes
2	
3	Read: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/remote-client.md` (all 553 lines), `docs/lessons.md`, the "Remote client" status section of `docs/design.md` (3107–3583; the file is 3678 lines, I did not read the rest), and the code named below. Line numbers are from this worktree (HEAD 7fe8949, Release 0.4.1). Nothing was run, built or tested.
4	
5	## 1. The on-disk record and its rehydration (before the pane)
6	
7	The issue adds **no new durable record**. The page is a view over records that exist; the one durable thing it touches is the device record.
8	
9	- **Device record.** `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`): `id`, `name`, `scope`, `token_sha256`, `created`, `last_seen`. Stored in `<data dir>/devices.json` through `RemoteFiles::save_devices` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:83`). Only the SHA-256 of the token is kept. A browser is one more row. Issue decision 6 (name from the user agent, listed and revocable) needs no schema change: the name is the `device_name` string `/pair` already takes (`src/app.rs:3650`, truncated to 64 chars in `new_device`, `src/core/remote.rs:~150`). Nothing records that a device is a browser, or which credential kind it holds. If the plan wants "browser" shown in the dialog, that is a new field on `PairedDevice` (`#[serde(default)]` keeps old files readable; `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` is a different file). Whether devices.json needs a version bump is open.
10	- **Rehydration at start.** `load_identity` (`src/app.rs`, near 2975) reads `identity.json` and `devices.json`, fetches the key from the secret store, and dispatches `AppAction::IdentityLoaded`. A device and its scope survive a restart; a token stays valid because its hash is on disk. So a browser paired yesterday is authenticated today by whatever credential it kept. A missing key remakes the identity and clears `devices.json` (`remote-client.md` §3.1, §5; test `a_missing_key_at_start_remakes_the_identity_and_clears_the_devices`, `tests/remote.rs:1422`). The page must then show "identity changed, pair again" for a browser whose stored key hash no longer matches `/info`.
11	- **Credential on the browser's side** (not the host's record): a bearer token held by the page, or an `HttpOnly` cookie holding it. Either way the host rehydrates by hashing it and calling `device_by_token` (`src/core/remote.rs:~118`). The pairing window itself (`PairingWindow`, code, scope, failures) is in memory only and never saved; that stays.
12	- **Live state the page shows** is rebuilt by the protocol's own subscribe-then-snapshot (`remote-client.md` §4.4): `hello`, then the snapshots, then the buffered events reconciled by revision. The page keeps everything in memory (the spec's "client keeps content in memory only", §7). A reload refetches. The page's only persisted bit is its credential (see Q on cookie vs `localStorage`) and possibly the host key it was paired with.
13	- **Static assets** are compiled in (`include_str!`/`include_bytes!`). No file on disk to rehydrate. The tree has `include_bytes!` only for fonts and an icon (`src/ui/theme.rs:203`, `src/main.rs:167`), so no `web/` directory or embedded-page precedent exists yet. Release notes need a `CHANGELOG.md` line under Unreleased.

15	## 2. Where the code is
16	
17	### The listener and request parsing — `src/adapters/remote.rs`
18	- `RemoteRequest` (`:360`): `method`, `path`, `query`, `body`, `bearer`, `upgrade`. No `User-Agent`, `Cookie`, `Origin`, `Host`, `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, `If-None-Match` fields.
19	- `read_request` (`:444`): lowercases header names, but **keeps only** `content-length`, `authorization` (must start `Bearer `), `upgrade` and `sec-websocket-key`. Everything else is parsed and discarded. Query values are undecoded (`:495`–`503`), documented as "ids and numbers only": a pairing URL's `key`/`id`/`code` are not read here (they go to the page), but a percent-encoded query would not be decoded by this parser.
20	- `respond` (`:530`): **hard-codes `Content-Type: application/json`**, `Connection: keep-alive`, no other header, and a fixed status-reason table (200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 413, 429, 503, 504). A page, a `Set-Cookie`, a CSP, `Cache-Control`, a 304 or a 101 with a subprotocol header cannot be sent without changing this. `RemoteReply` (`:389`) is `{status, body, authenticated}`: it has no content type or header slot.
21	- `respond_upgrade` (`:519`): writes the 101 with `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` only, no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`. A browser that offered a subprotocol requires the server to echo one or it fails the socket.
22	- Pools and limits: `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`, `MAX_PAIRED = 12` (`:567`); `HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` 5 s, `IDLE_TIMEOUT` 30 s, `WRITE_TIMEOUT` 10 s (`:570`–`574`); `PAIR_PER_MINUTE = 6`, `INFO_PER_MINUTE = 60` (`:583`); `Limits::limited` (`:631`) rate-limits **only** `/api/v1/pair` and `/api/v1/info` by exact path match. The accept loop (`:694`–`721`) closes a connection at once when 4 unauthenticated ones exist, **before** any request is read, so there is no way yet to tell a page load from a probe at accept time. A connection leaves the unauthenticated pool only when the frame's reply has `authenticated: true` (`:835`–`849`).
23	- `connection` (`:770`): every request, whatever the path, is `try_send` to the frame (`:810`). A static file would cost a frame pass (one frame interval, per `remote-client.md` §10 results) and take one of 64 inbox slots and one of the 8 per-pass drains (`DRAIN_PER_PASS`, `:580`) unless the connection thread answers it directly.
24	- `subscriber` (`:878`): the events socket; non-blocking, queue 256; text frames from the device (`watch`/`unwatch`) go to the frame as `SubscriberFrame`.
25	- `local_address` (`:962`): the one routed outward; `None` with no network.
26	- Certificate: `make_identity` (`:95`) builds `CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())`, i.e. **no subjectAltName**, CN `Switchboard <server id>`, `rcgen` default validity. The native clients pin SPKI so never needed names; a browser does (see Q).

28	### The frame side — `src/app.rs`
29	- `serve_pending` drain (`:1575`–`1600`): polls 8 requests per pass and calls `serve_remote`.
30	- `serve_remote` (`:3017`): **the allowlist.** `strip_prefix("/api/v1/")` or `404 not_found` via `refuse` (`:3023`). Unauthenticated: `GET info`, `POST pair` only (`:3029`–`3032`). Then `authenticate` (`:3128`): **bearer header only**; no cookie path; no bearer is a 401 `unauthorized` "pair this device first"; an unknown token is 401 "the token is not known; pair again". Revocation therefore shows to the page as a 401 with that message and the same code as "never paired"; there is no distinct `revoked` code. (`authenticate` also dispatches `DeviceSeen` on every request.)
31	- The routes the page needs already exist: `GET projects`, `GET projects/{id}/sessions`, `GET sessions/{id}`, `GET waiting`, `GET sessions/{id}/last-response`, `GET sessions/{id}/screen`, `POST sessions/{id}/send`, `GET events` (`:3040`–`3105`; content routes via `remote_content_route`, `:1947`). `send` and the others go through `remote_command` (`:3159`), body `{op, ...}` with the op the idempotency key; control scope is checked there.
32	- `remote_subscribe` (`:2723`): requires `request.upgrade`; `Subscriber{id, queue, device, all}` (`:242`); `RevokeDevice` handling in `dispatch_inner` (`:486`) drops the device's subscribers, which closes their sockets. A revoked browser's open WebSocket closes; the browser's close event carries no reason text from this path.
33	- `remote_info` (`:3568`): `server_id`, `server_name`, `protocol`, `capabilities`, `spki_sha256`, `version`, `limits`, `pairing_open`. It does **not** say whether the caller is paired or its scope/host name beyond `server_name`. The issue's "the device's scope in the header" needs the page to learn its own scope: the `/pair` reply has `scope` (`:3660`) but a returning browser (no `/pair`) has no call that returns its own scope or device name. Candidates are an extra field on an authenticated reply or a new endpoint; neither exists today.
34	- `remote_pair` (`:3606`): requires an open window, then JSON body `{spki_sha256, code, device_name}`; wrong key or wrong code each call `PairingFailed` (3 closes the window, `src/core/remote.rs:~44`); the reply is `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}` in the usual envelope. The token is in the JSON body. No `Set-Cookie`.
35	- `refuse` (`:3754`): logs method, path, code only (no query, so a `?code=` would not be logged by this line; the other log lines were not audited).
36	- Subscribers receive events as JSON text; the envelope fields in `event_json`; `hello` first.

60	## 3. Shape of the change, as the tree allows it (not a plan)
61	
62	- Adapter: a second kind of reply (non-JSON body, content type, extra headers) and a way to answer a static path either on the connection thread (before the frame, outside `RemoteIncoming`) or on the frame. The allowlist comment in `serve_remote` (`:3014`–`3016`) and `remote-client.md` §4.1/§5 ("Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused", "nothing but `/info` and `/pair` before pairing") are the sentences that change.
63	- Auth: whichever credential carrier is chosen must be accepted in `authenticate` (`:3128`), and `RemoteRequest` must carry it, since `read_request` drops cookies today. The native bearer path must stay.
64	- Pairing URL: `src/ui/remote.rs:161` payload and the Swift `PairingInvite.parse` (`Info.swift`) and the CLI's `pair` argument (`main.swift:107`). A URL form is parseable on both sides without JSON, but the Swift side would be a new parser and an `addresses` list does not fit a URL with one authority (only one address fits).
65	- Docs: `remote-client.md` §4.1, §4.3, §5 and the Milestone list; `docs/design.md` "Remote client" status section (ends at ~`:3583`); README Layout (`web/`, new files), `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased; possibly a spike (`spikes/*/README.md`) for browser behaviour per CLAUDE.md ("add a new spike directory for any new risky mechanism before building on it"). The WebSocket-credential mechanism and the certificate trust on iOS/Safari are such mechanisms.
66	- Hard-rule interactions to carry: no keystroke injection/osascript for testing a browser; tmux only on the test socket; the page and any fixture must not name a client; commit/PR text carries no tool attribution (CLAUDE.md overrides the harness reminder to add trailers); secrets never in URL or logs.

68	## 4. Things the issue says that this tree contradicts or does not support
69	
70	- "The pairing window's QR … a QR carrying `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`": true (`src/ui/remote.rs:161`).
71	- "Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused": true (`:3023`, 404).
72	- "the one-line excerpt the card shows": not on the wire (above).
73	- "the device's scope and host name in the header": host name is in `/info` (`server_name`); the scope is only in the `/pair` reply; nothing answers a returning device.
74	- "revoked states said plainly": the host answers a revoked token with the same 401 / `unauthorized` as an unknown one (`:3128`–`3156`); the message text differs only for no-token vs unknown-token. A revoked token is indistinguishable from a never-valid token because only hashes of live tokens are kept.
75	- "§5's rule that no non-loopback bind serves anything but `/info`, `/pair`": the spec text is `remote-client.md:306` ("Require pairing before anything but `/info` and `/pair`") and `:319`; and the UI checkbox hover text (`src/ui/remote.rs:~126`) says "only paired devices get past /info". Both say what the issue says to keep, with the page added.
76	- "§4.1 allows four unauthenticated connections": true, `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` (`:567`). Nothing counts a keep-alive connection that finished loading the page and sits idle for up to `IDLE_TIMEOUT` (30 s).
77	- "`/api/v1/events` WebSocket with the revision counter and `changed` events": true. Note the events URL accepts `?scope=all` as a query parameter, so query handling exists for the WebSocket path.
78	- Issue says the page may "post `send`"; the body shape is `{op, ...}` (control port `Body::Send`), op required (`serve`, `:3772`+). The page must make a UUID op per send and use `/ops/{op}` on timeout per §4.5. A page that is reloaded mid-send loses its op unless it keeps one.

120	[run] Do the existing `cargo test --locked --workspace` and `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass on this tree as a baseline (not run; the tree is clean per git status)?
121	[owner] Which trust step: the certificate click-through on the local network, said in the paired-devices dialog, or offering the certificate for download so the owner can install and trust it on the device first (decision 1)? Installing a profile on iOS is a device-and-account action, and trust of a user-installed certificate in Settings is a manual step the owner has to be willing to do; this is a call on taste and risk.
122	[owner] Cookie versus `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` for the credential (decision 2), and `localStorage` versus cookie for where the token lives: a call on how much XSS/CSRF surface the owner accepts on a page that can send text into a coding agent.
123	[owner] One URL QR or two (decision 3): is the JSON form kept for the CLI and the headset's paste, or does the Swift side move to the URL (and is the Swift client's tests-not-in-CI gap acceptable for that change)?
124	[owner] Is a page-served-on-pairing-before-trust acceptable to the owner given that a LAN impostor can serve a page that asks for the code (the issue says so itself): does the owner want the dialog to say this, and does the owner want the "waiting" reply box to exist at all on first release (control scope in a browser)?
125	[owner] Which devices and browsers must the acceptance be shown on (a phone camera, an iPad, another Mac) and with which iOS version; only the owner has the devices to confirm "scan the QR with a phone, accept the certificate warning, see the sessions".
126	[owner] The excerpt: is a new additive `SessionView` field (a masked one-line excerpt computed on the host) acceptable, or must the page fetch `last-response` per session (decision on the issue's "no new read model unless the page cannot do without one")? Also whether the excerpt must be masked the same way as every other text leaving the port (it is derived from the conversation, which the port masks only through the content worker).
127	[owner] The browser-device name: what the owner wants shown for a browser pairing when the user agent is unhelpful (a name typed on the page before pairing, versus derived from the user agent), and whether a browser device should be marked as such in the dialog.
128	[owner] Whether this feature needs a signed bundle test (Keychain ACL and the stable signing identity from `scripts/bundle.sh`) or is checkable with the throwaway data dir and socket; and whether the owner wants a spike directory first (CLAUDE.md asks for one for new risky mechanisms) before any page code.
129	----
130	# Spikes
131	
132	Throwaway crates and scripts that answered the Spike 0 questions in
133	`docs/design.md` before any product code was written. Each directory has a
134	README with the commands run, their output, and a recommendation. They are
135	kept for reference and are not built by the main crate.
136	
137	| Dir | Question | Answer |
138	| --- | --- | --- |
139	| `01-claude-resume` | Can Claude Code sessions be captured and resumed? | Yes: `--session-id <uuid>` at launch, `--resume <uuid>` later from any terminal. Transcripts pruned after 30 days unless `cleanupPeriodDays` is raised. |
140	| `02-process-host` | tmux or own PTYs? | tmux on a private server: sessions outlive the app, reattach works, ~3 ms round trip. PTY adapter kept as fallback and for tests. |
141	| `03-session-state` | How to know "waiting on you"? | Claude Code hooks (`PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`) via a tiny `switchboard-hook` binary and a Unix socket; OSC 777 text from the raw stream as the hook-free fallback. |
142	| `05-keychain` | Can secrets live in the Keychain without prompts? | Yes for a bundle signed with a stable identity and identifier: the item ACL is `identifier + certificate`, so rebuilds read silently. Ad-hoc builds prompt per rebuild. |
143	| `06-pane-size` | Why is the embedded pane wider than the widget? | `window-size manual` ignored the client; `latest` makes the window follow whichever client attached last. Re-applied on launch for servers that outlive the app. |
144	| `07-clone-session` | Can a session be cloned up to a chosen message? | Yes: copy the transcript prefix before the chosen prompt, substitute a fresh UUID for `sessionId`, save it `0600` beside the original; `--resume <new>` opens the truncated history and the original is untouched. |
145	| `08-promptbox-embed` | Can Prompt Box be the agent message box? | Yes: same egui 0.36, drawn into a bottom panel unchanged, a `Clipboard` adapter turns Send into a hand-off; needs an embedded mode, a sink port, and focus-scoped shortcuts in promptbox. |
146	| `09-popout` | Can a session live in a window of its own? | Yes: an immediate viewport drawn from the main frame holds the page, terminal, and side panel; its frame is saved to settings and restored. |
147	| `10-nunchuk-serial` | Can a nunchuk drive the working set over USB serial? | Yes: one line per button change or stick flick from the Feather, read on a thread that reconnects; round trip 2 to 9 ms. Firmware in `firmware/nunchuk`. |
148	| `11-gate-sandbox` | Can Dispatch's pipeline commands be confined to the ticket's tree on macOS? | Yes: `sandbox-exec` with `(allow default)`, writes denied except the tree, the attempt directory, the lane's caches and a base set; ~5 ms start-up; a refused write is `EPERM` and a tagged `deny(1)` line in the unified log. `setuid` programs and keychain creation fail inside it. |
149	| `12-hidden-frames` | Does the frame loop keep running while the window is occluded or minimized? | Not before the fix: with the app hidden, a control query timed out after 10 s and was answered at once on unhide. With the tick and `pump` in `App::logic`, hidden queries answer in 75 to 103 ms (eframe's 100 ms throttle for invisible windows). The sleep and wake cycle is not yet measured. |
150	| `13-dispatch-service` | Can a Dispatch service be a Switchboard service session, and how is its port read? | Yes: `$SHELL -lc 'exec "$@"' dispatch-service env PORT=<port> npm start` finds `npm`, answers (CRA in 27 s), and is gone with its port 200 ms after `kill-session`. A port is free only if `0.0.0.0`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` all bind: CRA listens on `*`, which a loopback bind does not see. |
151	| `14-env-exec` | Do a pane's record id and launch token reach a child, so `switchboard-env exec` can resolve its sets? | Yes for a shell grandchild of a tmux pane started with `-e`; the binary's path is covered by `tests/control.rs`. The `aws-vault` form and the no-prompt run under Dispatch's launch flags were not run and are left to the owner. |
152	| `15-paste-buffer` | Can a multi-line send be bracketed only for a pane that asked for it? | Yes: `load-buffer -` then `paste-buffer -p -r -d` frames the text in `ESC[200~` .. `ESC[201~` for a pane with `bracket_paste_flag` 1 and delivers it bare otherwise; `-r` keeps LF, `-d` leaves no buffer. CR passes through and tmux 3.7c shows ESC as a literal `^[`, so the sender turns CR into LF and removes ESC. `send-keys -H` passes the markers to every pane. Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
153	| `16-base-pipeline` | Can Dispatch find a merged pull request's merge commit and read the base's pipeline on it? | GitHub, yes: `mergeCommit` on `gh pr list` and `gh pr view`, and the commit's `check-runs` (a short hash works) show the base's run in progress and then finished. Bitbucket's reads were not run (the token could not be read in the run); the adapter follows the documented `merge_commit.hash`, commit `statuses` and pipeline `steps`, with a read by number when a list row lacks the commit; until they are run, a wait on a Bitbucket base pipeline is refused. |
154	| `18-tmux-argv` | Do `new-session -e` values show in a process listing, and can they reach tmux another way? | Yes, they did: the server keeps the argv of the client that started it. `tmux start-server \; source-file -` with the `new-session` line on stdin keeps every value and the pane command off any argv; cold and warm both work, errors still return, and double-quoted values with `\n` for line breaks round-trip (single quotes lose a line starting with `#`). Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
155	| `19-structured-ask` | Does a card's answer to a structured ask reach interactive Claude Code as the next user message, sent once, both at the prompt and when held until the turn's `Stop`? | Yes: `Owner answered "<question>": <answer>`, typed as one line, arrived as its own user message once in both cases; a held answer went out only after the `Stop`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.293 by the ignored gate test `a_structured_answer_arrives_as_the_next_prompt`. |
156	| `21-evidence-writes` | Which writes reach a stage's evidence directory, outside the agent's cwd, without a prompt? | The Write tool, under the attempt directory's `Edit(//<dir>/**)` rule. Bash `cp`, `mv` and `mkdir` ask, and `--add-dir` does not change that. A Playwright MCP screenshot is refused outside the server's roots unless it runs with `--allow-unrestricted-file-access`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.295 and `@playwright/mcp@0.0.82`. |
157	| `22-remote-port` | Can a pinned-TLS HTTP and WebSocket port run on std with every request answered by the frame thread, and what does it cost? | Yes: `rustls` + `rcgen` + `tungstenite` + `mdns-sd`, no Tokio; the frame's share is under 0.25 ms per pass, latency is one frame interval, the pools and the subscriber overflow hold under a stall and an unread socket, Bonjour is seen by `dns-sd`. A 146 MB transcript parses in 290 ms at 575 MB peak, so content work leaves the frame thread. ctime and inode see the file changes mtime and size miss. |
158	| `04-terminal-view` | Embedded terminal or hand-off? | Hand off agents to Ghostty (`open -na Ghostty --args ... -e cmd`, raise by title); embed `egui_term` for shells, commands, services. |

# Issue #230: a web control surface on the remote port — investigation notes

Read: `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/remote-client.md` (all 553 lines), `docs/lessons.md`, the "Remote client" status section of `docs/design.md` (3107–3583; the file is 3678 lines, I did not read the rest), and the code named below. Line numbers are from this worktree (HEAD 7fe8949, Release 0.4.1). Nothing was run, built or tested.

## 1. The on-disk record and its rehydration (before the pane)

The issue adds **no new durable record**. The page is a view over records that exist; the one durable thing it touches is the device record.

- **Device record.** `PairedDevice` (`src/ports/remote.rs:96`): `id`, `name`, `scope`, `token_sha256`, `created`, `last_seen`. Stored in `<data dir>/devices.json` through `RemoteFiles::save_devices` (`src/adapters/remote.rs:83`). Only the SHA-256 of the token is kept. A browser is one more row. Issue decision 6 (name from the user agent, listed and revocable) needs no schema change: the name is the `device_name` string `/pair` already takes (`src/app.rs:3650`, truncated to 64 chars in `new_device`, `src/core/remote.rs:~150`). Nothing records that a device is a browser, or which credential kind it holds. If the plan wants "browser" shown in the dialog, that is a new field on `PairedDevice` (`#[serde(default)]` keeps old files readable; `IDENTITY_SCHEMA_VERSION` is a different file). Whether devices.json needs a version bump is open.
- **Rehydration at start.** `load_identity` (`src/app.rs`, near 2975) reads `identity.json` and `devices.json`, fetches the key from the secret store, and dispatches `AppAction::IdentityLoaded`. A device and its scope survive a restart; a token stays valid because its hash is on disk. So a browser paired yesterday is authenticated today by whatever credential it kept. A missing key remakes the identity and clears `devices.json` (`remote-client.md` §3.1, §5; test `a_missing_key_at_start_remakes_the_identity_and_clears_the_devices`, `tests/remote.rs:1422`). The page must then show "identity changed, pair again" for a browser whose stored key hash no longer matches `/info`.
- **Credential on the browser's side** (not the host's record): a bearer token held by the page, or an `HttpOnly` cookie holding it. Either way the host rehydrates by hashing it and calling `device_by_token` (`src/core/remote.rs:~118`). The pairing window itself (`PairingWindow`, code, scope, failures) is in memory only and never saved; that stays.
- **Live state the page shows** is rebuilt by the protocol's own subscribe-then-snapshot (`remote-client.md` §4.4): `hello`, then the snapshots, then the buffered events reconciled by revision. The page keeps everything in memory (the spec's "client keeps content in memory only", §7). A reload refetches. The page's only persisted bit is its credential (see Q on cookie vs `localStorage`) and possibly the host key it was paired with.
- **Static assets** are compiled in (`include_str!`/`include_bytes!`). No file on disk to rehydrate. The tree has `include_bytes!` only for fonts and an icon (`src/ui/theme.rs:203`, `src/main.rs:167`), so no `web/` directory or embedded-page precedent exists yet. Release notes need a `CHANGELOG.md` line under Unreleased.

## 2. Where the code is

### The listener and request parsing — `src/adapters/remote.rs`
- `RemoteRequest` (`:360`): `method`, `path`, `query`, `body`, `bearer`, `upgrade`. No `User-Agent`, `Cookie`, `Origin`, `Host`, `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, `If-None-Match` fields.
- `read_request` (`:444`): lowercases header names, but **keeps only** `content-length`, `authorization` (must start `Bearer `), `upgrade` and `sec-websocket-key`. Everything else is parsed and discarded. Query values are undecoded (`:495`–`503`), documented as "ids and numbers only": a pairing URL's `key`/`id`/`code` are not read here (they go to the page), but a percent-encoded query would not be decoded by this parser.
- `respond` (`:530`): **hard-codes `Content-Type: application/json`**, `Connection: keep-alive`, no other header, and a fixed status-reason table (200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 405, 413, 429, 503, 504). A page, a `Set-Cookie`, a CSP, `Cache-Control`, a 304 or a 101 with a subprotocol header cannot be sent without changing this. `RemoteReply` (`:389`) is `{status, body, authenticated}`: it has no content type or header slot.
- `respond_upgrade` (`:519`): writes the 101 with `Sec-WebSocket-Accept` only, no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`. A browser that offered a subprotocol requires the server to echo one or it fails the socket.
- Pools and limits: `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED = 4`, `MAX_PAIRED = 12` (`:567`); `HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT` 5 s, `IDLE_TIMEOUT` 30 s, `WRITE_TIMEOUT` 10 s (`:570`–`574`); `PAIR_PER_MINUTE = 6`, `INFO_PER_MINUTE = 60` (`:583`); `Limits::limited` (`:631`) rate-limits **only** `/api/v1/pair` and `/api/v1/info` by exact path match. The accept loop (`:694`–`721`) closes a connection at once when 4 unauthenticated ones exist, **before** any request is read, so there is no way yet to tell a page load from a probe at accept time. A connection leaves the unauthenticated pool only when the frame's reply has `authenticated: true` (`:835`–`849`).
- `connection` (`:770`): every request, whatever the path, is `try_send` to the frame (`:810`). A static file would cost a frame pass (one frame interval, per `remote-client.md` §10 results) and take one of 64 inbox slots and one of the 8 per-pass drains (`DRAIN_PER_PASS`, `:580`) unless the connection thread answers it directly.
- `subscriber` (`:878`): the events socket; non-blocking, queue 256; text frames from the device (`watch`/`unwatch`) go to the frame as `SubscriberFrame`.
- `local_address` (`:962`): the one routed outward; `None` with no network.
- Certificate: `make_identity` (`:95`) builds `CertificateParams::new(Vec::<String>::new())`, i.e. **no subjectAltName**, CN `Switchboard <server id>`, `rcgen` default validity. The native clients pin SPKI so never needed names; a browser does (see Q).

### The frame side — `src/app.rs`
- `serve_pending` drain (`:1575`–`1600`): polls 8 requests per pass and calls `serve_remote`.
- `serve_remote` (`:3017`): **the allowlist.** `strip_prefix("/api/v1/")` or `404 not_found` via `refuse` (`:3023`). Unauthenticated: `GET info`, `POST pair` only (`:3029`–`3032`). Then `authenticate` (`:3128`): **bearer header only**; no cookie path; no bearer is a 401 `unauthorized` "pair this device first"; an unknown token is 401 "the token is not known; pair again". Revocation therefore shows to the page as a 401 with that message and the same code as "never paired"; there is no distinct `revoked` code. (`authenticate` also dispatches `DeviceSeen` on every request.)
- The routes the page needs already exist: `GET projects`, `GET projects/{id}/sessions`, `GET sessions/{id}`, `GET waiting`, `GET sessions/{id}/last-response`, `GET sessions/{id}/screen`, `POST sessions/{id}/send`, `GET events` (`:3040`–`3105`; content routes via `remote_content_route`, `:1947`). `send` and the others go through `remote_command` (`:3159`), body `{op, ...}` with the op the idempotency key; control scope is checked there.
- `remote_subscribe` (`:2723`): requires `request.upgrade`; `Subscriber{id, queue, device, all}` (`:242`); `RevokeDevice` handling in `dispatch_inner` (`:486`) drops the device's subscribers, which closes their sockets. A revoked browser's open WebSocket closes; the browser's close event carries no reason text from this path.
- `remote_info` (`:3568`): `server_id`, `server_name`, `protocol`, `capabilities`, `spki_sha256`, `version`, `limits`, `pairing_open`. It does **not** say whether the caller is paired or its scope/host name beyond `server_name`. The issue's "the device's scope in the header" needs the page to learn its own scope: the `/pair` reply has `scope` (`:3660`) but a returning browser (no `/pair`) has no call that returns its own scope or device name. Candidates are an extra field on an authenticated reply or a new endpoint; neither exists today.
- `remote_pair` (`:3606`): requires an open window, then JSON body `{spki_sha256, code, device_name}`; wrong key or wrong code each call `PairingFailed` (3 closes the window, `src/core/remote.rs:~44`); the reply is `{token, scope, server_id, device_id}` in the usual envelope. The token is in the JSON body. No `Set-Cookie`.
- `refuse` (`:3754`): logs method, path, code only (no query, so a `?code=` would not be logged by this line; the other log lines were not audited).
- Subscribers receive events as JSON text; the envelope fields in `event_json`; `hello` first.

### The pairing window — `src/ui/remote.rs`, `src/core/remote.rs`
- `src/ui/remote.rs:155`–`215`: builds the JSON payload `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}` (`:161`–`166`), `addresses` = `["<ip>:<port>"]` or empty, from `remote::local_address()` and `cx.remote_port.unwrap_or(identity.listen.port)`; `qr_texture` (`:280`) with `qrcode::QrCode::new`; "Copy invite" (`:204`) puts the same JSON on the clipboard. The key is also shown as `short_hash` (first 16 hex digits in groups of four).
- The dialog text says "Scan, or type the key and the code." A URL QR changes what a camera app does with it (it opens the browser), which is the point, but then a native client scanning it gets a URL.
- Only one address is put in the payload; the dialog also shows `Address ip:port`. With the port on loopback (`listen.lan == false`) the address is still the LAN IP, which then refuses connections. Not a new issue but the page URL inherits it.
- `core/remote.rs`: `OpenPairing{code, scope}`, `PairingFailed`, `Paired`, `RevokeDevice`, `SetDeviceScope`, `new_device` (takes the scope from the window). Pairing logic is core-side and deterministic; nothing in it knows what kind of client paired.
- The existing UI test `remote_devices_dialog_opens_pairing_and_revokes_a_device` is at `tests/ui.rs:7424`. It asserts on the dialog, not on the QR payload (I did not read its body, so whether it asserts the payload text is unchecked).

### The text pairing path that must keep working — Swift
- `client/Sources/SwitchboardProtocol/Info.swift` (`PairingInvite`, ~`:90`–`117`): `Decodable` with `server_id`, `spki_sha256`, `code`, `addresses`; `parse(_:)` is `Wire.decode(PairingInvite.self, from: Data(text.utf8))`, i.e. **JSON only**; a URL string would throw.
- `client/Sources/switchboard-remote/main.swift`: usage lines 12–13; `pair` (`:107`–`125`) takes either `'<invite json>'` (as one argument, `PairingInvite.parse(rest[0])`) or `<host:port> <code> <spki_sha256>`. So the CLI parses text. The headset's paste fallback uses the same `PairingInvite.parse` (design.md says "Pasting the invite's text stays as the fallback"; I did not find the SwiftUI call site because my grep for `PairingInvite` outside `Info.swift` errored on a shell glob and I did not repeat it).
- README says `switchboard-remote pair "$(pbpaste)"` pairs from the copied invite (README near `:277`).
- The Swift tests are not in CI or the pre-commit hook (design.md A2 status). A change to `PairingInvite.parse` is not exercised by `cargo test`.

### What the headset/CLI does that the page would copy
- The "last response" the Swift browser shows comes from `GET sessions/{id}/last-response` (`BrowserView.swift:35`, `:153`, via `manager.lastResponse`).
- **The "one-line excerpt the card shows" is not a wire field.** The Mac computes it in the UI: `agent_excerpt` (`src/ui/cards.rs:558`): first non-empty line of the last turn's `final_text`, else the last activity line, else `You: <prompt>`, clipped to 160 chars; non-agent kinds use `state.captions` (screen text). `SessionView` (`control/src/lib.rs:637`) has no excerpt, no `last_message`. (`last_message` exists only in the hook log and core tests.) `remote-client.md` §4.3 says the card's excerpt is "`last_message` from the `Stop` hook … a field of the session's metadata"; the code does not match that sentence. So the issue's "each with its kind, state and the one-line excerpt the card shows" implies either one `last-response` fetch per session (N requests per list view, each through the content worker and watch set, cap 128 keys) or a new additive field on `SessionView`, which the issue says to avoid ("No new read model unless the page cannot do without one"). The hash for the fingerprint diff is derived on `SessionView`, so adding a field moves `changed` frames.

### Tests and fixtures
- `tests/remote.rs` (3592 lines): `http()` at `:245` is a **raw TLS client over `rustls` pinned to the host key**, sending `Authorization: Bearer`, reading `Content-Length`, returning only status + body (it drops response headers). It parses `Content-Length` only with the exact casing `Content-Length:` (`:~287`). So header assertions (CSP, Content-Type, Cache-Control, Set-Cookie) need a new helper that returns headers. `call` drives `serve_pending` on the test thread while a client thread requests (`:299`). `pair` helper at `:406`. Subscriber helpers `subscribe` etc. at `:1932`–`2062`. Fixtures written by `write_fixtures` (`:1587`) with `SWITCHBOARD_WRITE_FIXTURES=1` and decoded on both sides at `:1829`.
- Allowlist test: `the_allowlist_refuses_everything_else_with_no_side_effect` (`:682`). `info_is_served_to_anyone_and_every_other_read_is_refused_unpaired` (`:426`) will need amending when `GET /` stops being refused. `stalled_strangers_fill_their_own_pool_and_never_a_paired_clients` (`:3226`) pins the 4-connection behaviour.
- `tests/ui.rs` has no browser. There is no `web/`, no JS toolchain, no headless browser in the tree. The issue's own wording ("no UI test drives a browser") agrees.

## 3. Shape of the change, as the tree allows it (not a plan)

- Adapter: a second kind of reply (non-JSON body, content type, extra headers) and a way to answer a static path either on the connection thread (before the frame, outside `RemoteIncoming`) or on the frame. The allowlist comment in `serve_remote` (`:3014`–`3016`) and `remote-client.md` §4.1/§5 ("Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused", "nothing but `/info` and `/pair` before pairing") are the sentences that change.
- Auth: whichever credential carrier is chosen must be accepted in `authenticate` (`:3128`), and `RemoteRequest` must carry it, since `read_request` drops cookies today. The native bearer path must stay.
- Pairing URL: `src/ui/remote.rs:161` payload and the Swift `PairingInvite.parse` (`Info.swift`) and the CLI's `pair` argument (`main.swift:107`). A URL form is parseable on both sides without JSON, but the Swift side would be a new parser and an `addresses` list does not fit a URL with one authority (only one address fits).
- Docs: `remote-client.md` §4.1, §4.3, §5 and the Milestone list; `docs/design.md` "Remote client" status section (ends at ~`:3583`); README Layout (`web/`, new files), `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased; possibly a spike (`spikes/*/README.md`) for browser behaviour per CLAUDE.md ("add a new spike directory for any new risky mechanism before building on it"). The WebSocket-credential mechanism and the certificate trust on iOS/Safari are such mechanisms.
- Hard-rule interactions to carry: no keystroke injection/osascript for testing a browser; tmux only on the test socket; the page and any fixture must not name a client; commit/PR text carries no tool attribution (CLAUDE.md overrides the harness reminder to add trailers); secrets never in URL or logs.

## 4. Things the issue says that this tree contradicts or does not support

- "The pairing window's QR … a QR carrying `{server_id, spki_sha256, code, addresses}`": true (`src/ui/remote.rs:161`).
- "Any path outside `/api/v1/` is refused": true (`:3023`, 404).
- "the one-line excerpt the card shows": not on the wire (above).
- "the device's scope and host name in the header": host name is in `/info` (`server_name`); the scope is only in the `/pair` reply; nothing answers a returning device.
- "revoked states said plainly": the host answers a revoked token with the same 401 / `unauthorized` as an unknown one (`:3128`–`3156`); the message text differs only for no-token vs unknown-token. A revoked token is indistinguishable from a never-valid token because only hashes of live tokens are kept.
- "§5's rule that no non-loopback bind serves anything but `/info`, `/pair`": the spec text is `remote-client.md:306` ("Require pairing before anything but `/info` and `/pair`") and `:319`; and the UI checkbox hover text (`src/ui/remote.rs:~126`) says "only paired devices get past /info". Both say what the issue says to keep, with the page added.
- "§4.1 allows four unauthenticated connections": true, `MAX_UNAUTHENTICATED` (`:567`). Nothing counts a keep-alive connection that finished loading the page and sits idle for up to `IDLE_TIMEOUT` (30 s).

# Spikes

Throwaway crates and scripts that answered the Spike 0 questions in
`docs/design.md` before any product code was written. Each directory has a
README with the commands run, their output, and a recommendation. They are
kept for reference and are not built by the main crate.

| Dir | Question | Answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `01-claude-resume` | Can Claude Code sessions be captured and resumed? | Yes: `--session-id <uuid>` at launch, `--resume <uuid>` later from any terminal. Transcripts pruned after 30 days unless `cleanupPeriodDays` is raised. |
| `02-process-host` | tmux or own PTYs? | tmux on a private server: sessions outlive the app, reattach works, ~3 ms round trip. PTY adapter kept as fallback and for tests. |
| `03-session-state` | How to know "waiting on you"? | Claude Code hooks (`PermissionRequest`, `Stop`, `SessionEnd`) via a tiny `switchboard-hook` binary and a Unix socket; OSC 777 text from the raw stream as the hook-free fallback. |
| `05-keychain` | Can secrets live in the Keychain without prompts? | Yes for a bundle signed with a stable identity and identifier: the item ACL is `identifier + certificate`, so rebuilds read silently. Ad-hoc builds prompt per rebuild. |
| `06-pane-size` | Why is the embedded pane wider than the widget? | `window-size manual` ignored the client; `latest` makes the window follow whichever client attached last. Re-applied on launch for servers that outlive the app. |
| `07-clone-session` | Can a session be cloned up to a chosen message? | Yes: copy the transcript prefix before the chosen prompt, substitute a fresh UUID for `sessionId`, save it `0600` beside the original; `--resume <new>` opens the truncated history and the original is untouched. |
| `08-promptbox-embed` | Can Prompt Box be the agent message box? | Yes: same egui 0.36, drawn into a bottom panel unchanged, a `Clipboard` adapter turns Send into a hand-off; needs an embedded mode, a sink port, and focus-scoped shortcuts in promptbox. |
| `09-popout` | Can a session live in a window of its own? | Yes: an immediate viewport drawn from the main frame holds the page, terminal, and side panel; its frame is saved to settings and restored. |
| `10-nunchuk-serial` | Can a nunchuk drive the working set over USB serial? | Yes: one line per button change or stick flick from the Feather, read on a thread that reconnects; round trip 2 to 9 ms. Firmware in `firmware/nunchuk`. |
| `11-gate-sandbox` | Can Dispatch's pipeline commands be confined to the ticket's tree on macOS? | Yes: `sandbox-exec` with `(allow default)`, writes denied except the tree, the attempt directory, the lane's caches and a base set; ~5 ms start-up; a refused write is `EPERM` and a tagged `deny(1)` line in the unified log. `setuid` programs and keychain creation fail inside it. |
| `12-hidden-frames` | Does the frame loop keep running while the window is occluded or minimized? | Not before the fix: with the app hidden, a control query timed out after 10 s and was answered at once on unhide. With the tick and `pump` in `App::logic`, hidden queries answer in 75 to 103 ms (eframe's 100 ms throttle for invisible windows). The sleep and wake cycle is not yet measured. |
| `13-dispatch-service` | Can a Dispatch service be a Switchboard service session, and how is its port read? | Yes: `$SHELL -lc 'exec "$@"' dispatch-service env PORT=<port> npm start` finds `npm`, answers (CRA in 27 s), and is gone with its port 200 ms after `kill-session`. A port is free only if `0.0.0.0`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]` all bind: CRA listens on `*`, which a loopback bind does not see. |
| `14-env-exec` | Do a pane's record id and launch token reach a child, so `switchboard-env exec` can resolve its sets? | Yes for a shell grandchild of a tmux pane started with `-e`; the binary's path is covered by `tests/control.rs`. The `aws-vault` form and the no-prompt run under Dispatch's launch flags were not run and are left to the owner. |
| `15-paste-buffer` | Can a multi-line send be bracketed only for a pane that asked for it? | Yes: `load-buffer -` then `paste-buffer -p -r -d` frames the text in `ESC[200~` .. `ESC[201~` for a pane with `bracket_paste_flag` 1 and delivers it bare otherwise; `-r` keeps LF, `-d` leaves no buffer. CR passes through and tmux 3.7c shows ESC as a literal `^[`, so the sender turns CR into LF and removes ESC. `send-keys -H` passes the markers to every pane. Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
| `16-base-pipeline` | Can Dispatch find a merged pull request's merge commit and read the base's pipeline on it? | GitHub, yes: `mergeCommit` on `gh pr list` and `gh pr view`, and the commit's `check-runs` (a short hash works) show the base's run in progress and then finished. Bitbucket's reads were not run (the token could not be read in the run); the adapter follows the documented `merge_commit.hash`, commit `statuses` and pipeline `steps`, with a read by number when a list row lacks the commit; until they are run, a wait on a Bitbucket base pipeline is refused. |
| `18-tmux-argv` | Do `new-session -e` values show in a process listing, and can they reach tmux another way? | Yes, they did: the server keeps the argv of the client that started it. `tmux start-server \; source-file -` with the `new-session` line on stdin keeps every value and the pane command off any argv; cold and warm both work, errors still return, and double-quoted values with `\n` for line breaks round-trip (single quotes lose a line starting with `#`). Measured on tmux 3.7c. |
| `19-structured-ask` | Does a card's answer to a structured ask reach interactive Claude Code as the next user message, sent once, both at the prompt and when held until the turn's `Stop`? | Yes: `Owner answered "<question>": <answer>`, typed as one line, arrived as its own user message once in both cases; a held answer went out only after the `Stop`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.293 by the ignored gate test `a_structured_answer_arrives_as_the_next_prompt`. |
| `21-evidence-writes` | Which writes reach a stage's evidence directory, outside the agent's cwd, without a prompt? | The Write tool, under the attempt directory's `Edit(//<dir>/**)` rule. Bash `cp`, `mv` and `mkdir` ask, and `--add-dir` does not change that. A Playwright MCP screenshot is refused outside the server's roots unless it runs with `--allow-unrestricted-file-access`. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.295 and `@playwright/mcp@0.0.82`. |
| `22-remote-port` | Can a pinned-TLS HTTP and WebSocket port run on std with every request answered by the frame thread, and what does it cost? | Yes: `rustls` + `rcgen` + `tungstenite` + `mdns-sd`, no Tokio; the frame's share is under 0.25 ms per pass, latency is one frame interval, the pools and the subscriber overflow hold under a stall and an unread socket, Bonjour is seen by `dns-sd`. A 146 MB transcript parses in 290 ms at 575 MB peak, so content work leaves the frame thread. ctime and inode see the file changes mtime and size miss. |
| `04-terminal-view` | Embedded terminal or hand-off? | Hand off agents to Ghostty (`open -na Ghostty --args ... -e cmd`, raise by title); embed `egui_term` for shells, commands, services. |
